rationale: Roberts is likely to keep the opinion narrow and institutional, holding that FSIA’s civil-action framework does not strip § 3231 criminal jurisdiction, while reserving any residual common-law/comity immunity questions. Kagan or Thomas are the main alternatives given their central framing (civil end-run precedents/Samantar and textual limits to “nonjury civil action[s]”), with separate concurrences most likely from Thomas or Gorsuch to emphasize textualism and the limited role of common-law immunity.
